title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
keyIdea: Use the BST order: if p and q are both smaller than the node, go left; both bigger, go right. The first node where they split (or that equals one of them) is the LCA. One path down: O(h).

approaches.name: Any binary tree (search both sides)
approaches.idea: Return p or q when you hit one; ask both subtrees; if both sides found something, this node is the LCA, else pass up whichever side found one.
approaches.why: Ignores the BST order, so it may visit every node. Works for LC 236 (plain binary tree).

approaches.name: BST walk
approaches.idea: Both smaller → recurse left. Both bigger → recurse right. Otherwise return root.
approaches.why: Only one path from the root is followed. h = log n when balanced. (Written as a loop it would be O(1) space.)
